mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the ultimate corporate shareholder (PRC parent company)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), People's Republic of China
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PRC notary public notarization, then single Hague Apostille by the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs or provincial foreign affairs office if the destination is an Apostille Contracting State; for Taiwan use cross-strait verification through ARATS/SEF, and never chain Hague Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), People's Republic of China
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PRC notary public notarization, then single Hague Apostille for Apostille-convention destinations; for Taiwan use cross-strait notarization and ARATS/SEF verification only; consular legalization is not applied in the PRC-Taiwan channel.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney appointing the Taiwan incorporator and local compliance officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: PRC parent company board of directors, notarized by a PRC notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized board resolution; attach one Hague Apostille if used in an Apostille state; for Taiwan use cross-strait verification through ARATS/SEF, with no subsequent consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), People's Republic of China
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy from SAMR, notarized in PRC, then one Hague Apostille for Apostille state use; for Taiwan use cross-strait notarial copy verified by ARATS/SEF; never chain apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the PRC parent's principal settlement account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: PRC commercial bank maintaining the parent company settlement account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank-issued letter on bank letterhead, notarized by a PRC notary; for Apostille destinations attach one Hague Apostille; for Taiwan use cross-strait verification; do not add consular legalization unless the destination treaty regime specifically requires it, in which case use consular legalization alone.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must cover all shareholders with at least 25% equity, directors, supervisors, final beneficial owners, and senior managers. Screen against UN Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, the PRC PBOC/SAMR UBO register, Taiwan FSC designated terrorist and money-laundering lists, and domestic prominent public official databases. Politically exposed persons, their families, and close associates require enhanced due diligence. Use World-Check, Dow Jones Risk Center, or equivalent daily updated risk intelligence, match fuzzy transliteration, alias, and low-threshold phonetic variants, and document all adverse hits. Unresolved PEP or sanctions hits are an absolute filing rejection trigger.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Company and Commerce Registration Information System and Company Name Pre-Review System, Department of Commercial Services, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be filed in Mandarin Chinese with Traditional Chinese script, with a permitted English transliteration on the registration record if desired. The statutory four-tier naming convention requires: tier 1, a distinctive brand or transliterated name; tier 2, a business-scope descriptor sufficient to avoid public confusion; tier 3, risk-sensitive tokens requiring FSC/MOEA approval; and tier 4, the mandatory limited-company legal-form suffix. English names, if registered, must be a direct transliteration or romanisation of the Chinese name and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon MOEA name rejection, the applicant must extract the written rejection reasons from the Company Name Pre-Review System, then file an administrative appeal with MOEA within 30 days. The appeal must include a revised distinctive name, evidence of non-conflict from the registry search, trademark office search results, and a legal memorandum addressing each prohibited or sensitive token. MOEA must issue a written determination within 45 days. If denied, the applicant may file an administrative action at the Taipei High Administrative Court. During appeal, a fresh name reservation should be filed immediately after the prior reservation expires to protect market position.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a licensed equity crowdfunding portal in Taiwan, a virtual office or mailbox-only address is not acceptable. The Financial Supervisory Commission, MOEA, and Taiwanese banks will reject the license and escrow account applications because the AML risk tier is High_Risk_Special_License. A physical Taiwan office with locally hosted books and records, on-site compliance personnel, and electronic data access is mandatory. A virtual office may only be used for ancillary correspondence after physical-office verification.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Inspection checklist: physical lease or ownership deed; presence of employees during business hours; statutory books, meeting minutes, shareholder register and UBO register at the registered office; name plate matching the registry; and secure access for tax and FSC examiners. Quantified risk: unannounced joint inspection probability is above 35% in the first 12 months after a crowdfunding license is issued, and below 10% for an ordinary non-licensed registration unless a complaint or AML alert is filed.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Republic of China (Taiwan) Company Act (公司法), Articles 1, 2, 4, 7, 8, 12, 27, 28, 128, 153, 156, 172, 192, 203, 204, 208, 228, 235, 237, 387, and 449; Regulations on Registration of Companies (公司之登記及認許辦法), Articles 2-13; Foreign Investment Regulations (華僑及外國人投資許可辦法).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (經濟部), Department of Commerce, Company Registration and One-Stop Service Division.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation Registration of a Company Limited by Shares (股份有限公司設立登記申請書), submitted with the Articles of Incorporation, Incorporation Meeting Minutes, and Directors'/Supervisors' Consent to Serve.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital for companies limited by shares under Article 156 of the Company Act. Paid-in capital must be fully subscribed and deposited into a domestic bank account in the company's name before registration. A CPA-issued capital verification report is mandatory. For equity crowdfunding portals, the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) may impose an operating guarantee deposit and stricter escrow rules under securities regulations, which are licensing requirements rather than general corporate capital rules. No blocked escrow account is required by the Companies Act for ordinary incorporation, but investor funds must be segregated in an escrow account under FSC crowdfunding rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME], a company limited by shares incorporated under the Republic of China (Taiwan) Company Act. The undersigned directors, constituting a quorum, hereby adopt the following resolutions: 

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND VERIFICATION: RESOLVED that the Board acknowledges receipt of the capital contribution certificates, bank deposit certificates, and CPA capital verification report demonstrating that the entire authorized share capital of [amount] New Taiwan Dollars, divided into [number] shares at par value [amount] each, has been fully subscribed and paid in cash by the shareholders. The Board confirms that the funds remain on deposit at [bank name and branch] under account number [account number] and shall not be withdrawn except for lawful corporate purposes following incorporation.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED that the following persons, [Director A], [Director B], and [Officer C], be and are hereby appointed as authorized signatories for all banking, borrowing, and escrow transactions of the Company. Any two of such persons acting jointly shall have authority to open or close accounts, execute loan agreements, sign checks, direct wire transfers, and operate the Company's escrow account designated for investor funds. RESOLVED FURTHER that the FSC-required investor escrow account shall be maintained separately from operating accounts and shall be governed by the escrow agreement approved by the FSC.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company shall be located at [full address in Taiwan], which the Board ratifies as the statutory address for service of process, and the Company Secretary is authorized to register such address with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and to post the required company signboard in accordance with Article 28 of the Company Act.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: RESOLVED that [name] is appointed Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer; [name] is appointed Company Secretary; [name] is appointed Chief Financial Officer; and [name] is appointed Chief Compliance Officer with responsibility for FSC licensing, anti-money-laundering, and investor protection oversight. RESOLVED FURTHER that the Chairman and Company Secretary, acting jointly, are authorized to execute all incorporation, licensing, and regulatory filings on behalf of the Company.

5. INCORPORATION AND REGULATORY FILING: RESOLVED that the officers are directed to prepare and file the incorporation registration application with the MOEA, obtain the unified business tax number, register with the labor authorities, and thereafter apply for the FSC equity crowdfunding portal license. All prior acts performed in good faith for the Company before this resolution are hereby ratified.

There being no further business, the meeting is adjourned. Certified by the Chairman this [day] day of [month], [year].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Pre-Approval and Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) and MOEA One-Stop Company Registration Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before filing the incorporation application, foreign investors must obtain foreign investment approval under the Foreign Investment Regulations. Submit the Application for Foreign Investment Approval with passport/entity certificates, source of funds, and a business plan for the equity crowdfunding portal. Simultaneously, reserve the proposed company name (Chinese and English) via the MOEA Company Name Reservation System. The name must not conflict with any existing registered entity or prohibited keyword. The foreign investment approval certificate and name reservation certificate are mandatory preconditions for the final incorporation filing. All foreign-language documents must be translated into traditional Chinese by a certified translator and notarized as required.
required_dossiers: Passport or entity certificate of each foreign shareholder
Certificate of incorporation and board resolution of corporate shareholder
Power of attorney appointing Taiwan agent/attorney
Business plan for equity crowdfunding operations
Proof of foreign investment approval fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a query, respond within 14 days with supplementary documents. If rejection occurs, file an administrative appeal within 30 days. Name reservation may be reapplied immediately with an alternative name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Deposit and CPA Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Trusted domestic Taiwan bank and a licensed Taiwan CPA registered with the FSC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary incorporation capital collection account in the company's proposed name. Each promoter/subscriber must deposit the full subscription amount in cash or wire transfer. The bank will issue a certificate of deposit. A Taiwan CPA must then perform a capital verification audit, confirming that the full paid-in capital has been received and remains unwithdrawn, and issue the Capital Verification Report. The report must be dated no more than 15 days before the incorporation filing. The account is frozen until the company is registered; after registration, it converts into the company's operating account. For a crowdfunding portal, ensure the FSC escrow arrangement for investor funds is separately documented.
required_dossiers: Bank deposit certificate or passbook for the capital account
Draft Articles of Incorporation for CPA review
Identity documents of directors and shareholders
Bank account application forms and company seal card
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CPA identifies capital deficiency, all subscribers must top up the difference and reverify. If any shareholder withdraws capital before registration, the deposit must be fully restored and verification restarted. If the bank queries source of funds, provide wire records and sponsor declarations to clear enhanced due diligence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Meeting, Articles Adoption, and First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Promoters, shareholders, and directors of the WFOE; witnessed by a Taiwan notary or attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the incorporation meeting at which promoters adopt the Articles of Incorporation, elect the first board of directors and supervisors, and approve the transfer of capital to the company. Immediately thereafter, convene the first board meeting and pass the formal board resolution covering share capital subscription, banking authorization, registered office, and officer appointments, as set out in the pro-forma resolution. The minutes of both meetings must be prepared in traditional Chinese, signed by the chairperson and secretary, and notarized if banks or authorities require. Appointees must sign consent-to-serve letters. The board chair must certify the Articles as a true copy.
required_dossiers: Consent to Serve forms for directors and supervisors
Subscription list and capital contribution records
Identification documents of all directors and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If meeting format is challenged, reconvene and re-adopt resolutions. Correct any defect in quorum or voting promptly. Notarization may be reissued. All documents must be re-executed if amendments are required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs Department of Commerce – Company Registration Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete incorporation registration package electronically via the MOEA One-Stop Online Registration System, or in person at the service counter. The application must include the Articles, incorporation meeting minutes, first board meeting minutes, capital verification report, foreign investment approval, consent-to-serve, registered office address proof, and name reservation certificate. The MOEA will verify statutory compliance and issue the Company Registration Certificate. Upon issuance, the company obtains its unified corporate identity and can proceed to tax registration. The filing fee of approximately USD 275 must be paid online. Registration occurs simultaneously with the issuance of the company's unified business tax number in the commercial registration system.
required_dossiers: Registered office address proof (lease or ownership + landlord consent)
Power of attorney for filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MOEA issues a deficiency notice, cure and resubmit within 15 days. If rejection occurs due to name conflict, reserve a new name and resubmit. Administrative appeal is available within 30 days. The filing fee may be forfeited if rejection is final; restart fee payment with new filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Labor Registration, and Corporate Seal Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau (Ministry of Finance), local Bureau of Labor Insurance, and local branch of MOEA or notary office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 14 days after MOEA registration, complete tax registration: register with the National Taxation Bureau for profit-seeking enterprise income tax and business tax, obtain the Unified Business Tax Number and invoice usage authorization. Register as a withholding agent for employee income tax. Under labor law, register with the Bureau of Labor Insurance for labor insurance, health insurance, and pension plans before hiring staff. Also prepare the company seal and representative's seal; have the seal card notarized or witnessed by the bank and MOEA for use in banking and legal documents. For foreign-owned entities, file the foreign investment report with the FSC Investment Commission for tax and balance-of-payments statistics. After these registrations, the company may legally issue invoices and hire employees.
required_dossiers: Corporate seal card and proof of seal
Bank account opening certificate for operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is delayed, pay late filing penalties and submit supplementary. If the tax bureau disputes business scope, amend Articles and refile. Any labor inspection discrepancy must be cured immediately. Appeal adverse determinations to the Executive Yuan or the administrative court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: FSC Equity Crowdfunding Portal License Application and Compliance Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC), Securities and Futures Bureau
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a comprehensive special license application to the FSC for operating as an equity crowdfunding portal under ISIC 6499. The application must include corporate records, authorized business scope, AML/CFT compliance program, internal control procedures for issuer due diligence, investor qualification checks, fund custody agreement with an escrow bank, IT security systems, and disaster recovery plan. Provide proof of paid-in capital and any FSC-prescribed operational guarantee deposit. A board resolution must designate the chief compliance officer and adopt policies against fraud, money laundering, and investor loss. The FSC will conduct a full review and may conduct an on-site inspection. Upon approval, a license will be issued; the portal may then commence solicitation of equity crowdfunding offerings.
required_dossiers: Escrow agreement with bank for investor funds
Information security and cyber resilience audit report
Board resolution on compliance and officer appointment
Paid-in capital proof and guarantee deposit certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FSC requests supplements, respond within the given period or face rejection. If denied, correct deficiencies and resubmit after a waiting period. File administrative appeal within 30 days of final disposition. Maintain a legal and compliance advisor throughout the process.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) – Securities and Futures Bureau; Ministry of Economic Affairs; local municipal Department of Economic Development; National Fire Agency (NFA); local fire department.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Equity Crowdfunding Portal License (股權群眾募資平台許可證) under the Securities Investor and Futures Trader Protection Act and related FSC regulations; additionally, a Business Registration Certificate from the MOEA/FSB tax authority.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Taiwan Environmental Protection Administration (EPA) and local Municipal Environmental Protection Bureau
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category E – Self-Declaration / Environmental Registration for Digital and IT service portals. Since the primary business is a digital intermediary with no physical manufacturing, chemical processing, or warehousing, a full EIA Report is not required. However, a self-certification of environmental compliance and waste disposal registration is mandatory. If any physical back-office, data center, battery storage, or backup generator is installed, a Category B Environmental Impact Assessment Analysis may be required depending on capacity thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: sanitary sewage only; must comply with municipal sewer discharge standards under the Water Pollution Control Act, with pH 6-9, biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) below 300 mg/L, chemical oxygen demand (COD) below 500 mg/L, and suspended solids below 300 mg/L. VOCs: office air-conditioning and cleaning operations must not emit volatile organic compounds beyond the Taiwan indoor air quality standard of 0.15 ppm for total VOCs in workplace air. Hazardous waste: spent batteries, electronic equipment, and any e-waste must be collected and disposed through EPA-approved vendors; manifest documents retained for 5 years. No industrial process wastewater is generated.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety: Obtain a Fire Safety Device Inspection Certification from the local fire department for office premises, including smoke detectors, fire extinguishers, emergency lighting, and evacuation signage. For server rooms, a fire suppression system (clean agent) is recommended and a building usage permit confirming structural suitability must be secured. Occupational safety: Register with the Occupational Safety and Health Administration, submit a workplace self-inspection report, and designate a safety and health officer if employee count exceeds 30. IT security and physical access controls must be maintained as part of the FSC license requirement.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Republic of China (Taiwan) – National Taxation Bureau; online portal: https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity establishing a Taiwan wholly foreign-owned enterprise (WFOE) limited liability company, the entity must first complete company registration with the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA). Within 15 days of commencing business, the company must apply for Business Tax Registration (營業稅籍登記) with the local National Taxation Bureau. Required documents include the company incorporation certificate, articles of incorporation, and identification of the responsible person. The bureau issues a Unified Business Number (TIN) as the statutory tax identification. For foreign entities without a local establishment but engaging in taxable activities, a VAT representative must be appointed and registration completed before the first taxable transaction.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None – Taiwan does not provide check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections; all limited liability companies are taxed at the entity level under the Income Tax Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NT$200,000 monthly sales (or NT$2.4 million annual) for goods and services; mandatory registration for businesses exceeding this threshold. Financial services, including equity crowdfunding portals, are subject to the same threshold unless otherwise exempted.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan mandates the use of electronic invoices (電子發票) for businesses with annual sales exceeding NT$30 million. These invoices must be transmitted to the Ministry of Finance's E-Invoice Platform (電子發票整合服務平台) within 48 hours of issuance. The platform requires API integration and uses a unique invoice number and QR code for anti-fraud verification. For high-risk industries, including financial intermediaries, real-time clearance may be required. Non-compliance results in penalties under the Business Tax Act.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and services are zero-rated under Article 7 of the Business Tax Act. For goods, the goods must be physically exported from Taiwan and a customs export declaration must be filed. For services, including equity crowdfunding portal services, the services must be provided to foreign clients, used outside Taiwan, and the consideration must be received in foreign currency. The service provider must maintain evidence of the foreign client's identity, the service contract, and proof of foreign currency receipt.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or Foreign Exchange Receipts (for services)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If zero-rating is claimed without proper documentation, the tax authority may impose a penalty of up to 5 times the tax evaded, plus interest. Retrospective clawback of zero-rated treatment is possible, and fraudulent claims may lead to criminal prosecution under the Tax Evasion Act, with imprisonment and fines.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The People's Bank of China (PBOC), acting through the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: RMB is convertible on the current account for genuine cross-border receipts and payments, including services, dividends, and profit remittances, subject to SAFE declaration and tax clearance. The capital account, by contrast, remains tightly controlled: every inbound equity injection from the Taiwan parent requires an FDI foreign exchange registration, a dedicated Foreign Exchange Capital Account at a licensed bank, and payment-based conversion into RMB strictly for the WFOE's approved operating uses. There is no automatic right for non-residents to invest or withdraw funds without SAFE registration, and no offshore alternative such as a fintech EMI can lawfully perform onshore RMB clearing or capital FX settlement for a Chinese legal entity. The WFOE must demonstrate real business substance, maintain full documentation of each remittance, and use the domestic banking system for conversion, payroll, procurement, and profit distribution. Profit repatriation to the Taiwan shareholder is permitted only after the annual audit, required reserve allocations, corporate income tax payment or exemption certificate, board approval, and SAFE current-account filing. Taiwan-side receipt may also be subject to the Taiwan Central Bank's cross-border remittance reporting threshold, but that reporting obligation does not alter SAFE's onshore controls. Convertibility is thus open for genuine current items but unavailable for speculation, synthetic RMB offshore structures, or unrestricted hedging on the capital account.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE's prevailing trade foreign-exchange rules, export proceeds in foreign currency must be repatriated into China within 180 days from the date of customs export declaration, or within the extended contractual payment period where SAFE grants permission. The WFOE/exporter must report the receipt in the Trade Foreign Exchange Monitoring System. There is no fixed mandatory conversion ratio; the exporter is permitted to retain 100% of export receipts in a current-account FX account or sell them to a licensed bank in exchange for RMB. Any conversion must reflect a genuine trade or service transaction, evidenced by contract, invoice, customs declaration or service transaction attestation, and the relevant SAFE transaction/purpose code.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Account and RMB Basic Deposit Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Crowdfunding Investor Escrow Account and Payment Settlement Account
Basic Operational Currency Account and estimated-tax clearing account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital banks and electronic-money institutions (EMIs) are legally barred from acting as the onshore settlement bank for a mainland Chinese WFOE. They cannot hold RMB deposits, operate a SAFE-registered Foreign Exchange Capital Account, perform capital verification, or execute the statutory FX conversion required for an equity crowdfunding intermediary. At best, an offshore EMI could be used on a non-banking basis to collect contributions from non-China crowd investors before routing the pooled funds through a licensed Tier-1 Chinese bank, but the EMI cannot replace the domestic treasury and clearing mandate. The WFOE should therefore enter into no primary custody or disbursement arrangement with any EMI.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-branch physical presence is mandatory for the statutory legal representative and at least one designated signatory when opening the RMB basic deposit account and any FX capital account. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not permitted as a complete solution, especially for a high-risk, statutorily licensed financial intermediary. Taiwan-issued corporate documents must be notarized, authenticated through the applicable cross-strait document verification process, and translated into Chinese by a certified translator before the bank's compliance committee will accept the KYC file.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The ultimate beneficial owner chain includes a Taiwan holding entity and natural-person founders, creating an opaque cross-strait ownership structure and possible shell/ownership concentration risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized certificate of incorporation and current director/shareholder register from the Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, certified Chinese translations, a complete group structure chart with ownership percentages, UBO declarations for every natural person holding 25% or more, 12 months of bank statements and tax returns for each intermediate holding entity, sworn source-of-wealth reports, and board resolutions approving the formation and capital plan of the WFOE.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The entity is an equity crowdfunding portal classified as an ISIC 6499 'other financial service' with a high-risk special license, raising third-party investor money and creating regulatory/licensing ambiguity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Statutory internet financial business license or provincial financial regulatory approval for equity crowdfunding, the CSRC/regional equity market admission or filing notice, the escrow agreement with a licensed Chinese bank, independent custodian confirmation letter, platform operating rules, AML/CFT internal control manual, designated AML compliance officer appointment, and a third-party legal/compliance opinion confirming the licensing boundary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commingling of investor crowdfunding funds with the WFOE's own operating capital could be used to launder third-party proceeds or facilitate rapid pass-through payments to unverified startup recipients.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Client fund segregation and escrow agreements, daily bank reconciliation statements, independent audit reports on internal controls over escrow, investor subscription agreements and identity/KYC files, project pitch decks and due-diligence approvals by the investment committee, disbursement authorization matrix, bank statements showing one-to-one matching of investor records to escrow movements, and sanctions/PEP screening logs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from Taiwan is in equity form and requires SAFE FDI registration; undeclared or unverified capital may be classified as illegal cross-border funds or disguising reinvestment.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign-investment filing/approval record from MOFCOM or local commerce authority, SAFE FDI foreign-exchange registration certificate for the WFOE, Taiwan bank remittance confirmation and SWIFT MT103 with the correct direct-investment purpose code, source-of-funds evidence from the Taiwan shareholder, CPA-issued capital verification report, board resolution authorizing the injection, and a written representation letter confirming the funds will be used only for approved operating purposes in the PRC.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwan shareholder must first complete the SAFE FDI registration for the WFOE and then remit equity funds by SWIFT MT103 to the WFOE's dedicated Foreign Exchange Capital Account at a Tier-1 Chinese bank. The remittance should carry the approved SAFE direct-investment purpose code for equity injection, and the remitter's reference field should include the FDI registration number. The receiving bank will log the transaction in SAFE's FDI and capital-account information system, verify the permitted business scope, and allow conversion into RMB on a payment-based, real-demand basis. A CPA capital verification report should be issued if required by the bank's internal policy or requested by the Taiwan investor. Funds may not be diverted to unapproved investments, securities, real estate, or loans without additional SAFE approval.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For cross-border treasury payments, including profit dividends, licensing fees, and refunds of surplus crowdfunding contributions to offshore investors, SWIFT MT103 is the standard rail. For domestic RMB settlement to startups, vendors, and statutory tax authorities, the WFOE should use the CNAPS High-Value Payment System and the electronic clearing system. Commercial Letters of Credit and Documentary Collections are not relevant to the crowdfunding core business; they may be used only if the WFOE undertakes incidental physical trade, and only with full trade documents (contract, invoice, transport documents and inspection certificates) to satisfy both the issuing bank and SAFE reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable CNY/USD forward exchange contracts concluded with a licensed Chinese bank under a documented genuine underlying FX exposure, physically settled and approved for SAFE reporting
Onshore RMB foreign-exchange swaps (spot/forward combinations) matched to current-account or permitted capital-account cashflow timing
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for medium-term onshore obligations where the underlying principal/interest schedule is proven and does not create a speculative open position

Structured RMB options or zero-cost collars only where the notional does not exceed the documented underlying FX exposure; non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible onshore and must not be booked by the WFOE

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting and approval of annual business report, financial statements, and earnings appropriation or loss-offsetting proposal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders as the internal corporate organ; records and minutes maintained at the registered office and, where a registrable resolution is passed, filed with the MOEA Department of Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the fiscal year-end; by 30 June for a calendar-year WFOE, unless an extension is expressly granted by the central competent authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible directors may be administratively fined NT$10,000 to NT$50,000; shareholders may petition to convene; prolonged failure may be treated as a governance failure leading to court or MOEA dissolution proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual filing of the audited financial statements and business report under Article 20 of the Companies Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the fiscal year-end; by 30 June for a calendar-year WFOE; the independent CPA report must precede filing when the WFOE meets any compulsory-audit threshold
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: MOEA may issue an enforcement order; continued non-compliance exposes responsible persons to administrative fines of NT$10,000 to NT$50,000 per violation and, on repeated default, administrative strike-off or compelled dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual profit-seeking enterprise income tax settlement return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the local tax region, Ministry of Finance (Taiwan)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year WFOE, 1 May to 31 May of the following year; for an approved non-calendar fiscal year, within five months after the fiscal year-end; statutory one-month filing extensions may apply only in prescribed circumstances
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing triggers a surcharge of 10% of the assessed tax with a minimum administrative fine, assessed underpayment penalties, and daily overdue interest at the Ministry of Finance rate; persistent non-payment may result in treasury attachment, asset seizure, and administrative collection

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual withholding tax and salary or rent paid-items summary statement for employees and non-residents
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the local tax region, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 January following the calendar year of payment, or within ten days after salary or non-resident payments cease
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Understatement or late filing subjects the WFOE to surcharges under the Income Tax Act, including up to twice the under-withheld amount in aggravated cases, interest, and suspension of tax-clearing certificates

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual equity crowdfunding portal regulatory compliance report, AML/CFT report, internal control statement, and audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC), Securities and Futures Bureau, and the competent securities or trade association as required by the license conditions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after fiscal year-end by 30 April for a calendar-year WFOE, and on the dates stated in the FSC license
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit may result in FSC administrative fines, public censure, restricted business operations, suspension of the portal, or revocation or expiration of the special license; AML/CFT deficiencies additionally attract penalties under the Money Laundering Control Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholder register, director register, charge register, and beneficial-ownership confirmation audit and 30-day transfer recording
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: MOEA Department of Commerce for registered particulars; the Financial Supervisory Commission for UBO and AML record inspection; internal statutory registers maintained at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the Annual General Meeting and at least once per calendar year; any share transfer or beneficial-ownership change is recorded in the statutory register within 30 days of the completion of the transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors or officers may be fined for refusing or neglecting register updates; false entries may attract criminal or falsification liability; a failure to maintain registers at the registered office is a distinct statutory default and may support MOEA strike-off action

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent certified CPA audit is mandatory if the WFOE has paid-in capital equal to or greater than NT$30 million; if annual turnover or revenue exceeds NT$100 million under MOEA or income-tax examination rules; if the company is a securities firm, equity crowdfunding portal, or special FSC-regulated business regardless of size; if required by the Investment Commission as a condition for foreign or Mainland-area invested enterprise approval; or if the WFOE elects Taiwan-IFRS. Headcount alone is not a Taiwan statutory audit trigger, but reaching 100 employees adds mandatory labor, pension, and welfare fund obligations that require separate annual filings.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan-IFRS as endorsed by the FSC for public issuers; for non-public companies, ROC Enterprise Accounting Standards, aligned with IFRS for SMEs, or full Taiwan-IFRS may be used consistently. The equity crowdfunding portal must follow the framework designated by its FSC license, normally full Taiwan-IFRS in audited financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At least once each calendar year and in any event at the Annual General Meeting, management must confirm and update the beneficial-ownership and shareholder register. Any transfer of shares or change of ultimate beneficial owner must be documented and recorded in the statutory registers within a maximum 30-day reporting window after closing; where a transfer alters directors, capital, or MOEA-registered particulars, the amendment must be filed with the MOEA within the statutory filing period. For the FSC-regulated equity crowdfunding portal, the UBO register and source-of-funds evidence must be available immediately for FSC inspection and updated continuously; the annual AML/CFT report must identify all greater-than-10% owners and senior-manager controllers.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $3,000-$9,000 per annum for a private WFOE with CPA audit; $8,000-$20,000 per annum for an FSC-regulated equity crowdfunding portal

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% corporate income tax (Income Tax Act Article 5), plus 5% surtax on undistributed retained earnings (Article 66-9)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday for equity crowdfunding platforms; available incentives: R&D investment tax credit up to 15% of qualifying expenditure (Statute for Industrial Innovation Article 10, capped at 30% of tax payable); preferential 12% corporate Alternative Minimum Tax (AMT) on taxable income above TWD 500,000 exemption; foreign tax credit on foreign-source income; credit for qualifying reinvestment in the Startup Act up to 20% for accredited investors and certain venture fund structures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Settlement Return (Form 15 series) filed through the Ministry of Finance electronic filing portal (tax.nat.gov.tw) using the entity's digital registration certificate or approved financial certificate; semi-annual provisional returns use the Profit-Seeking Enterprise Provisional Income Tax Return (Article 67 form).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return; semi-annual provisional estimated returns (first half installment due September 30; second half installment due March 31 of the following year for calendar-year filers).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return must be filed within 5 months after the fiscal year end (calendar-year entity: by May 31 of the following year); provisional estimated returns and payments are due no later than September 30 and March 31 respectively; audited financial statements follow the same 5-month statutory deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross operating revenue (crowdfunding platform fees, margin on services, escrow-related service income, and advisory fees).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Taiwan-sourced platform income only if attributable to a branch or permanent establishment in Taiwan; foreign-source commission income of a Taiwan resident WFOE is reportable with foreign tax credit claimed separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold and direct service costs (server hosting, licensing fees, payment processing expenses, due diligence contractor costs).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident branches deduct direct and allocable Taiwan-related expenses; no deduction for head-office overhead not supported by a cost allocation plan approved by the tax authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses (salaries, rent, AML compliance systems, internal audit costs, professional fees, depreciation).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be arm's length and properly documented; intercompany management fees to foreign headquarters require TP documentation and are deductible only when services actually benefit the Taiwan operation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (net amount after disallowed expenses such as fines, bribes, and non-business-related expenses).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities are taxed on Taiwan-source taxable income at 20%; no loss carryforward for offshore losses or non-incorporated offshore overhead.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable before credits (20% statutory rate applied to taxable income).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident branch profit remitted offshore is subject to additional 21% profit remittance withholding (treated as dividend distribution) unless treaty relief applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Investment tax credits (R&D and industrial innovation credits applied against tax payable).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credits are available to the Taiwan-registered entity regardless of foreign ownership; documentation requirements and credit caps of 30% of remaining tax apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit for income taxes paid to foreign jurisdictions on foreign-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credit limited to Taiwan tax attributable to that foreign-source income; excess credit is non-refundable; no domestic credit for taxes paid by foreign shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Basic tax under the Income Basic Tax Act (AMT) at 12% with TWD 500,000 exemption; addbacks include low-taxed offshore income and specific tax-exempt items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident branches with Taiwan-source income are also subject to AMT; an AMT return is required where regular tax is below the basic tax amount.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additional 5% surtax on unappropriated earnings for the year (subject to statutory deduction of TWD 50,000 and reinvestment reserves).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Surtax applies at the Taiwan entity level regardless of shareholder residence; subsequent dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders are separately subject to 21% withholding.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharge: 3% of the unpaid tax for each month or part-month, capped at 10% (minimum TWD 1,500); failure to file after notice: 3% surcharge (minimum TWD 3,000, cap 10%); late payment surcharge: 1% for every 2 days, capped at 10%; statutory interest accrues on overdue amounts; the responsible person may be subjected to compulsory execution, publication of delinquent taxpayers, and exit restriction where the confirmed delinquent tax exceeds the statutory threshold.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% withholding tax on gross dividends distributed by a Taiwan company to a non-resident corporate shareholder (Income Tax Act Article 88 and Article 73); dividends to resident corporate shareholders are exempt from withholding under Article 42.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced treaty dividend rate (usually 10% to 15%): (1) obtain a Tax Resident Certificate (TRC) from the foreign shareholder's home-country tax authority; (2) submit the 'Application for Application of Tax Agreement (Dividend/Interest/Royalty)' to the local National Taxation Bureau before the withholding event, attaching the TRC, a beneficial-ownership declaration, audited financial statements if requested, and proof of shareholding period; (3) the withholding agent may provisionally apply the treaty rate upon complete submission; (4) if the reduced rate is not applied at source, file a refund claim within 5 years of the original withholding date; the approval is generally granted on an event-by-event basis unless a standing approval has been obtained.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory non-resident rates: 20% for royalties and 20% for interest (Interest and Royalty Article 88); most Taiwan tax treaties reduce both to 10% (e.g., Taiwan-Netherlands, Taiwan-UK, Taiwan-Switzerland, Taiwan-Luxembourg treaties); a reduced treaty rate requires the same TRC and beneficial-ownership protocol; interest paid by the WFOE must not exceed arm's-length rates, otherwise the excess is recharacterized as a distribution subject to 21% withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File / Transfer Pricing Report is mandatory when total related-party transactions reach TWD 200 million or more in a tax year, or when cross-border related-party transactions reach TWD 50 million or more (small-taxpayer exemption applies when total related-party transactions are below TWD 20 million); Master File and Country-by-Country Report are required when the multinational group's consolidated annual revenue equals or exceeds TWD 27 billion; contemporaneous TP documentation must be prepared by the filing deadline and produced within 30 days of a tax authority request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan does not issue Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations; instead, the 'Actual Place of Effective Management' (PEM) doctrine and Controlled Foreign Company (CFC) rules (effective 1 January 2023) recapture income of offshore-interposed entities whose central management and control is exercised in Taiwan. For the equity crowdfunding portal, the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) license requires a substantive local office, at least two full-time compliance and risk-management officers, a locally maintained audit trail, and independent audit of custodial or escrow funds; failure to maintain this substance may cause the tax authority to ignore the separate legal personality of the WFOE, deny treaty benefits, recast escrow fees as Taiwan-source service income, and refer the matter to the FSC for license revocation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealment or underreporting of crowdfunding platform fees, issuance of fictitious or inflated invoices ('vain invoices') to shift profits, improper deduction of personal expenses, or diversion of escrow commission income to offshore shell accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Underpayment penalty of 1 to 3 times the evaded tax under Article 110 of the Income Tax Act; criminal liability under Article 41 of the Tax Collection Act: imprisonment up to 5 years and fine up to TWD 6 million; where the evaded amount exceeds TWD 25 million, imprisonment of 2 to 10 years and fine up to TWD 30 million; publication of the taxpayer and compulsory execution of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representative and directors may be personally and jointly liable for the company's unpaid tax and penalties where the evasion arises from deliberate corporate conduct; the tax authority may impose travel bans, detain the responsible person pending collection, and courts may order civil restitution to investors; serious fraud convictions can lead to imprisonment of directors and prohibition from serving as managers for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Taiwan WFOE with no physical office, no employees, no local bank account, no board meetings in Taiwan, or using the entity solely to hold a FSC license without real business activity; interposing an offshore holding company to obscure Taiwanese control of the crowdfunding platform.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the entity's income as directly earned by the beneficial owner under PEM/CFC rules; denial of tax treaty benefits; denial of deductions for offshore management fees; deregistration of the company under the Company Act for failure to maintain registered office; fines and revocation of the FSC license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors jointly and severally liable for restitutions and back taxes following the recharacterized assessment; travel bans and asset freezes under Article 24 of the Tax Collection Act when the confirmed tax exceeds statutory thresholds; disqualification orders for company management; criminal sanction for making false statutory declarations in the FSC license application.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the equity crowdfunding escrow and payment rails without appropriate customer due diligence (CDD), beneficial-ownership identification, ongoing transaction monitoring, or filing of Suspicious Transaction Reports; knowingly processing proceeds of fraud through the platform's escrow accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to TWD 5,000,000 under the Money Laundering Control Act per violation; administrative suspension or revocation of the FSC crowdfunding license; for disgraceful conduct, criminal money-laundering liability under Article 14 of the Act with imprisonment of up to 7 years and fines up to TWD 50,000,000; confiscation of illicit assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible persons who knowingly facilitate or fail to prevent money laundering face criminal imprisonment, personal fines, and confiscation of personal assets; directors may be barred from service in the financial sector for a period up to 10 years; exit restrictions and freeze orders are routinely imposed during investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Offering equity, profit-sharing interests, or tokenized revenue streams to the Taiwanese public without an FSC-issued securities license, or operating a crowdfunding portal beyond the scope of the securities broker approval, including unauthorized secondary-market trading of startup shares.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Securities and Exchange Act, unauthorized securities business is punishable by imprisonment of 2 to 10 years and a fine of TWD 2 million to TWD 20 million; the FSC may issue cease-and-desist orders, impose administrative fines, and order disgorgement of all profits received from the unlawful offering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, supervisors, and the legal representative bear joint civil liability to compensate defrauded investors; criminal imprisonment is imposed on responsible persons who knowingly operate without a license; the court may disqualify the individuals from serving as officers of any FSC-regulated entity and issue international travel bans pending subsequent collection or enforcement proceedings.
